## Remove Single-Option Decisions

There are a handful of decisions with only a single option, let's drop these to not throw off any of the algorithms.

```{r}
mv_siab_org |>
  get_multiverse_decisions()
```


```{r}
mv_siab <- mv_siab_org |> 
  remove_fake_decisions()
mv_siab
```

# Ablation Study

Fix each decision to one option, recompute the importance estimates on the
reduced multiverse, and compare the resulting importance vectors across
methods and across options of the fixed decision.

```{r}
ablation_siab <- run_ablation_analysis(
  mv_siab,
  colname_metric = "perf_acc"
)
```

## Stability across importance methods

The table below shows the baseline agreement between methods on the full
multiverse, plus the average agreement after fixing each decision and averaging
over that decision's options.

```{r}
ablation_siab$method_stability_summary |>
  mutate(
    fixed_decision_label = if_else(
      fixed_decision == "full_multiverse",
      "full multiverse",
      fixed_decision_label
    )
  ) |>
  select(
    fixed_decision_label,
    method_x,
    method_y,
    mean_rank_correlation,
    min_rank_correlation
  )
```

```{r}
vis_method_stability(ablation_siab$method_stability_summary)
```

## Does baseline importance predict option-induced change?

For each decision and method, compare the original full-multiverse importance
of that decision to the mean pairwise change in the ablated importance vectors
across the different fixed options of that decision.

```{r}
ablation_siab$option_sensitivity |>
  arrange(method, desc(baseline_importance)) |>
  select(
    fixed_decision_label,
    method,
    baseline_importance,
    mean_pairwise_abs_change,
    mean_pairwise_rank_correlation
  )
```

```{r}
ablation_siab$predictive_relationship
```

```{r}
vis_option_sensitivity(ablation_siab$option_sensitivity)
```
